events.title: The Hamdanids and Baridis fight for Baghdad at al-Mada'in
events.description: Near al-Mada'in in central Iraq, the armies of the Hamdanids of Mosul and the Baridis of Basra began a four-day battle for Baghdad, the Abbasid capital. The Hamdanids prevailed but were too exhausted to pursue, and the Baridis withdrew to Basra.

events.title: Nikephoros II Phokas is crowned Byzantine emperor
events.description: The general Nikephoros II Phokas was crowned emperor, swearing to protect the two sons of the late Romanos II, Basil II and Constantine VIII, who were already co-emperors. He was murdered by John Tzimiskes in 969.

events.title: The Gonzaga family takes power in Mantua
events.description: The House of Gonzaga seized power in Mantua, in Lombardy, beginning a rule that lasted until 1708. Under Federico II Gonzaga, its first duke, Mantua later became a duchy, which in 1531 also acquired Montferrat.

events.title: Henry VIII's army routs French cavalry at the Battle of the Spurs
events.description: English and imperial troops put French cavalry to flight near Guinegate, the speed of their retreat giving the battle its name. Thérouanne surrendered days later.

events.title: Cornwallis routs the Americans at Camden
events.description: British forces under Lord Cornwallis shattered Horatio Gates's army at Camden, South Carolina. The defeat led to Nathanael Greene taking command in the south.

events.title: Cavalry attack a reform meeting at Peterloo
events.description: Yeomanry and hussars charged a crowd of some 60,000 at St Peter's Field, Manchester, gathered to demand parliamentary reform. About 18 people died and hundreds were injured.

events.title: Gold is found on Bonanza Creek in the Klondike
events.description: George Carmack, Skookum Jim and Dawson Charlie struck gold on a tributary of the Klondike River in the Yukon. When news reached the south in 1897, some 100,000 people set out for the goldfields.

events.title: Elvis Presley dies at Graceland
events.description: Elvis Presley was found dead at his Memphis home, aged 42. The 'King of Rock and Roll' had sold hundreds of millions of records and transformed popular music.
